chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding the man who marries the woman by Mut'ah: 'They inherit each other as long as they did not stipulate (a time limit), and the stipulation is after the marriage.'
ai.seo_question: Do spouses in temporary marriage inherit from each other?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that in temporary marriage (Mut'ah), spouses automatically inherit from one another unless they explicitly stipulate otherwise, with the stipulation occurring post-contract. This ruling underscores the legal validity of Mut'ah as a full marital bond in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from mere concubinage by granting inheritance rights by default. The emphasis on post-nuptial stipulation highlights the flexibility and contractual nature of Mut'ah agreements within the Shia legal tradition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying regarding the man who marries the woman by Mut’a: ‘They would both be inheriting (each other) for as long as they did not stipulate, and rather the stipulation is after the marriage’ (as they ignored the condition of time so it has become more like a marriage).
